questions.question: A client is admitted with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. Which precaution is required?
options: Standard precautions only, because tuberculosis does not spread by close contact
Droplet precautions with a surgical mask
Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator and negative-pressure room
Contact precautions with gown and gloves and a dedicated stethoscope in the room
questions.explanation: TB spreads through airborne droplet nuclei. Airborne precautions require a fit-tested N95 (or higher) respirator and an airborne infection isolation room.

questions.question: Which infection requires droplet precautions?
options: Pertussis
Scabies
Measles
Clostridioides difficile
questions.explanation: Pertussis spreads by large respiratory droplets. C. difficile and scabies need contact precautions, and measles needs airborne precautions.

questions.question: After caring for a client with Clostridioides difficile, how should the nurse perform hand hygiene?
options: Hand hygiene isn't needed if gloves were worn
Use alcohol-based hand rub
Wash hands with soap and water
Wipe hands with a disinfectant wipe
questions.explanation: Alcohol doesn't reliably kill C. difficile spores. Washing with soap and water physically removes them.

questions.question: A fire starts in a client's room. Using the RACE acronym, what is the nurse's first action?
options: Contain the fire by closing doors and windows
Rescue clients in immediate danger
Extinguish the fire with the nearest extinguisher
Activate the alarm and call the operator
questions.explanation: RACE stands for Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish (or Evacuate). Removing clients from immediate danger comes first.

questions.question: When putting on personal protective equipment, which item does the nurse put on first?
options: Mask or respirator
Gloves
Goggles or face shield
Gown
questions.explanation: The CDC sequence for putting on PPE is gown, mask or respirator, goggles or face shield, then gloves.

questions.question: Which intervention is most effective for preventing falls in a confused older adult?
options: Keep the bed in the lowest position with the call light within reach
Keep the room dark at night so that the client will stay in bed and sleep soundly
Give a sedative at bedtime to reduce nighttime wandering and falls
Keep all four side rails up and leave the bed raised for easy care access
questions.explanation: A low bed, a call light within reach, and frequent rounding reduce fall risk. Four raised side rails count as a restraint and can increase injury risk.

questions.question: Before giving a medication, which pair of identifiers is acceptable?
options: Client's diagnosis and name
Room number and bed number
Name on the door and the client's response to their name
Client's name and date of birth
questions.explanation: Use at least two client-specific identifiers, such as full name and date of birth. Room numbers are never acceptable identifiers.

questions.question: A nurse gets a needlestick injury from a used needle. What is the first action?
options: Squeeze the site to make it bleed
Wait until the end of the shift to report it
Apply alcohol and continue working
Wash the area with soap and water
questions.explanation: Wash the site right away with soap and water, then report the exposure promptly so post-exposure evaluation and prophylaxis can begin.

questions.question: What is the minimum time the nurse should scrub hands when washing with soap and water?
options: 5 seconds
10 seconds
20 seconds
2 full minutes
questions.explanation: The CDC recommends rubbing hands with soap for at least 20 seconds.

questions.question: After giving a subcutaneous injection, what should the nurse do with the needle?
options: Put it in the regular trash
Recap it with both hands to prevent a stick
Place it in the sharps container without recapping
Bend it before discarding
questions.explanation: To prevent needlestick injuries, never recap, bend, or break used needles. Drop them directly into a puncture-resistant sharps container.

questions.question: A client uses home oxygen. Which statement shows that the teaching was understood?
options: "I'll store the tanks next to the heater to keep them warm and ready."
"I'll use petroleum jelly on my nose for dryness."
"I'll post a No Smoking sign and keep oxygen away from open flames."
"I can light candles if I keep them across the room from the oxygen."
questions.explanation: Oxygen supports combustion. Keep oxygen away from flames and heat, and use water-based lubricants instead of petroleum-based products.

questions.question: Which technique shows correct body mechanics when lifting?
options: Bending at the waist with straight knees to reach the object
Holding the object away from the body to keep the back straight
Twisting the trunk while lifting
Bending the knees and keeping the load close to the body
questions.explanation: Bend at the knees, keep a wide base of support, and hold the load close to the center of gravity to protect the back.

questions.question: A client is on contact precautions for MRSA. How should the nurse handle the stethoscope?
options: Share one stethoscope among all isolation rooms to save equipment costs
Use the nurse's personal stethoscope and wipe it afterward
Use a dedicated stethoscope that stays in the room
Auscultate over the gown without a stethoscope
questions.explanation: Dedicated, single-client equipment prevents the spread of organisms such as MRSA from room to room.

questions.question: Which precautions are used for a client with scabies?
options: Contact
Droplet
Airborne
Standard only
questions.explanation: Scabies spreads through direct skin contact and contaminated items, so contact precautions with gown and gloves are required.

questions.question: A chemical splashes into a coworker's eyes. What should the nurse do first?
options: Have the person rub the eyes to spread the tears and clear the chemical
Cover the eyes with a dry dressing and send the person to the ER
Flush the eyes with running water for at least 15 minutes
Apply an antibiotic ointment and cover both eyes with gauze
questions.explanation: Immediate, continuous irrigation with water for at least 15 minutes is the priority, followed by medical evaluation.

questions.question: The nurse's hands are not visibly soiled after taking a client's blood pressure. Which hand hygiene method is preferred?
options: Putting on gloves without hand hygiene
Alcohol-based hand rub
Wiping hands with a dry paper towel
Rinsing with water only
questions.explanation: When hands are not visibly soiled, an alcohol-based hand rub is the preferred method in most care situations. Soap and water are needed for visible soil and certain organisms such as C. difficile.

questions.question: Using the PASS method for a fire extinguisher, what is the first step?
options: Sweep from side to side
Pull the pin
Squeeze the handle
Aim at the base of the fire
questions.explanation: PASS stands for Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep. The pin must be pulled before the extinguisher can be used.

questions.question: A medication order reads "insulin regular 10 U subcutaneously." Why is this order a safety concern?
options: "U" is a do-not-use abbreviation that can be mistaken for 0 or 4
Insulin is never given subcutaneously because it is absorbed too slowly
Regular insulin is only given by mouth, never by injection or pump
The dose is missing a time and a frequency of administration
questions.explanation: "U" can be misread as 0 or 4, causing a tenfold error. The word "units" should be written out.

questions.question: A client has a latex allergy. Which foods may cause a cross-reaction and should be noted in the record?
options: Chicken, fish, and eggs
Bananas, avocados, and kiwi
Rice, oats, and wheat products
Milk, cheese, and yogurt
questions.explanation: Latex-fruit syndrome links latex allergy with reactions to foods such as banana, avocado, kiwi, and chestnut.

questions.question: A client on a medical unit has suspected norovirus gastroenteritis. Which precautions should the nurse use?
options: Standard precautions only with alcohol hand rub as the hand hygiene
Contact precautions with soap-and-water hand washing
Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator and negative-pressure room
Protective (reverse) isolation
questions.explanation: Norovirus spreads by contact and contaminated surfaces. Contact precautions are used, and soap and water work better than alcohol rub against it.

questions.question: A client is admitted with influenza. What protection does the nurse need when entering the room?
options: A surgical mask in addition to standard precautions
Sterile gown and gloves only
An N95 respirator and a negative-pressure room for every case
No extra protection if the nurse has been vaccinated against influenza
questions.explanation: Influenza is spread by droplets, so droplet precautions with a surgical mask are used along with standard precautions.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the 'time-out' performed just before a surgical procedure?
options: To document the anesthesia start time and the room temperature
To give the surgeon a moment to rest before starting
To count the sponges and instruments before the incision is closed
To confirm the correct client, procedure, and site as a team
questions.explanation: The time-out is a final check by the whole team to prevent wrong-site, wrong-procedure, and wrong-person surgery.

questions.question: The nurse notices that the power cord of an infusion pump is frayed. What should the nurse do?
options: Plug it into a different outlet and watch whether it sparks or smokes
Wrap the cord with tape and keep using it until the shift ends
Use it until the end of the shift and report it then
Remove the pump from use, label it, and report it for repair
questions.explanation: Damaged electrical equipment can cause shocks or fires. It must be taken out of service and reported to biomedical engineering.

questions.question: After discharge of a client with Clostridioides difficile infection, which product should be used to clean the room surfaces?
options: A sporicidal agent such as a bleach-based product
A fragrance spray to cover the odor and freshen the room
Plain soap and water only, followed by an air-dry
An alcohol-based disinfectant applied to all room surfaces
questions.explanation: C. difficile forms spores that resist alcohol. A sporicidal disinfectant, commonly a bleach-based product, is required.

questions.question: Before helping a client move from a bed to a wheelchair, what should the nurse do first?
options: Ask the client to stand quickly
Lock the wheelchair brakes and the bed wheels
Place the wheelchair at the foot of the bed facing away
Remove the footrests after the transfer is finished and the client is seated
questions.explanation: Locking the wheels on both the bed and the wheelchair keeps them from moving and prevents falls during the transfer.

questions.question: A client is admitted after exposure to inhalational anthrax. Which precautions are needed?
options: Droplet precautions
Airborne precautions
Protective isolation (reverse isolation)
Standard precautions
questions.explanation: Anthrax is not spread from person to person, so standard precautions are used. Decontamination is needed only if spores are on the skin or clothing.

questions.question: A client with a weakened immune system has disseminated herpes zoster. Which precautions should the nurse use?
options: Droplet precautions
Airborne and contact precautions
Standard precautions only
Contact precautions only
questions.explanation: Disseminated zoster requires airborne and contact precautions because the virus can spread through the air and by contact with lesions. These continue until all lesions are dry and crusted.

questions.question: A client with active pulmonary tuberculosis must be taken to radiology. Which action is correct?
options: The client wears a surgical mask during transport
The transport staff wear gowns only
The client wears an N95 respirator during transport
No mask is needed if the trip is short
questions.explanation: The client wears a surgical mask to contain droplet nuclei when outside the room. Staff in the client's presence wear fit-tested N95 respirators.

questions.question: Which room feature is required for a client on airborne precautions?
options: Negative air pressure with the door kept closed
A shared room with another infected client
A window kept open for fresh air
Positive air pressure compared with the hallway
questions.explanation: An airborne infection isolation room uses negative pressure with frequent air exchanges so air flows in rather than out into the hallway.

questions.question: Which action breaks the chain of infection at the 'mode of transmission' link?
options: Encouraging good nutrition
Performing hand hygiene between clients
Giving antibiotics for an infection that is already present
Vaccinating the client
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene stops germs from being carried from one person or surface to another, which is the mode of transmission.

questions.question: How should the PN carry soiled bed linens out of a client's room?
options: Shaken out before placing them in the hamper
Held against the chest and uniform so that they do not drop on the floor
Placed on the floor until the bed is made
Held away from the uniform and placed directly in the linen bag
questions.explanation: Holding linens away from the body and not shaking them prevents spreading microorganisms to the uniform and the air.

questions.question: When should a sharps container be replaced?
options: When the lid will no longer close because needles stick out
Once a month regardless of use
When it is about three-quarters full
Only when it is completely full
questions.explanation: Replacing sharps containers at about three-quarters full prevents overfilling, which can cause needlestick injuries.

questions.question: Before leaving a client's room, which safety action should the PN take?
options: Raise the bed to the highest position for the next caregiver
Move the walker across the room
Turn off all the lights
Place the call light within the client's reach
questions.explanation: Keeping the call light and personal items within reach helps clients get help without trying to get up alone.

questions.question: Which piece of protective equipment should the PN wear when there is a risk of blood splashing during wound irrigation?
options: A gown, gloves, mask, and eye protection
Shoe covers only
A hair cover only
Gloves only, because gloves protect against all body fluids
questions.explanation: Standard precautions include face and eye protection and a gown whenever splashes or sprays of body fluids are likely.

questions.question: What is the correct way to remove contaminated gloves?
options: Rinse them and then take them off carefully
Peel off the first glove at the wrist, then slide bare fingers under the second glove
Pull both gloves off together by the fingertips at the same time to save time in the room
Snap both gloves off by pulling hard at the fingertips so that they come off quickly together
questions.explanation: Glove-to-glove and skin-to-skin technique keeps the contaminated outer surface from touching bare skin.

questions.question: How often should a client in soft restraints be released, repositioned, and offered toileting?
options: Only when the client asks
Once per shift
At least every 2 hours
Every 6 hours
questions.explanation: Restraints are released at least every 2 hours for repositioning, range of motion, skin care, toileting, and fluids, with circulation checks more often per policy.

questions.question: Which infection is spread mainly by the fecal-oral route?
options: Hepatitis C
Hepatitis A
Tuberculosis
Hepatitis B
questions.explanation: Hepatitis A spreads through contaminated food, water, or hands. Hepatitis B and C spread through blood and body fluids.

questions.question: A client is on contact precautions. Which item should stay in the room?
options: The medication cart
The PN's personal stethoscope after each use
The PN's charting device
A disposable blood pressure cuff
questions.explanation: Dedicated or disposable equipment stays in the room to prevent spreading the organism. Shared equipment must be cleaned before use elsewhere.

questions.question: A client needs help walking for the first time after surgery. Which device should the PN use for safety?
options: A gait (transfer) belt
A rolling chair
A cane held in the weaker hand
A wrist restraint
questions.explanation: A gait belt lets the PN guide and support the client safely and reduces strain on the nurse's back.

questions.question: A client gets up to walk and says, "I feel dizzy and my vision is going gray." What should the PN do first?
options: Ask the client to hold their breath
Leave to get a wheelchair
Help the client sit or lower them safely to the floor
Tell the client to walk faster to the bed and sit down quickly
questions.explanation: Dizziness may signal orthostatic hypotension and a fall. The PN keeps the client from falling by helping them sit or by easing them to the floor.

questions.question: The parent of a toddler asks how to prevent poisoning at home. Which advice should the PN reinforce?
options: Tell the child medicine is candy so they will take it
Keep cleaning products under the sink in their original bottles
Store medicines and cleaners up high in locked cabinets
Put cleaning products in food containers to save space
questions.explanation: Locked, out-of-reach storage is the best prevention. Products should stay in original containers, and the Poison Help line number should be easy to find.

questions.question: Which instruction should the PN reinforce for a client who uses a heating pad at home?
options: Sleep with it on all night at a medium setting
Place it directly on the skin at the highest setting
Use it on numb areas of the feet and legs
Use a low setting and limit time, checking the skin often
questions.explanation: Heat can burn, especially in areas with poor sensation. Low settings, a cover, and time limits reduce the risk.

questions.question: A client with head lice is admitted. Which precautions should the PN use?
options: Protective isolation in a private room
Contact precautions until effective treatment
Droplet precautions with a surgical mask
Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator
questions.explanation: Head lice spread by direct contact and shared items such as combs and hats, so contact precautions are used until treatment is effective.

questions.question: Which action by the PN follows medical asepsis when caring for a client's wound?
options: Placing clean supplies on a clean surface and doing hand hygiene before and after
Placing used dressings on the bedside table until later
Cleaning from the dirty area toward the clean area of the wound
Reusing the same piece of gauze for cleaning the wound several times to save supplies
questions.explanation: Medical asepsis reduces the number and spread of microorganisms. Wounds are cleaned from the cleanest area outward, and used dressings go directly into a waste bag.

questions.question: A client's glucometer is shared on the unit. What should the PN do after using it?
options: Rinse it under running water and let it air-dry
Wipe it with a dry tissue before putting it away
Clean and disinfect it per the manufacturer's instructions
Put it back in the case without cleaning it
questions.explanation: Shared glucose meters can spread bloodborne viruses such as hepatitis B. They must be cleaned and disinfected between clients.

questions.question: The PN is reinforcing home safety teaching with the family of an older adult. Which statement shows understanding?
options: "We'll keep the hallway dim at night so Dad can sleep."
"We'll put a rug on the bathroom floor."
"We'll set the water heater to its highest setting so the bath stays hot."
"We'll test the smoke and carbon monoxide detectors regularly."
questions.explanation: Working detectors prevent deaths from fire and carbon monoxide. Lowering water heater temperature, adding light, and removing rugs also reduce injuries.

questions.question: A client with dementia is at risk of wandering. Which intervention should the PN suggest?
options: Keeping the client in a chair with a lap belt all day
An identification bracelet and an alarm on exit doors
Giving a sedative at the start of each shift to keep the client calm
Locking the client in the room
questions.explanation: Identification, door alarms, and supervision keep the client safe while avoiding unnecessary restraints or medications.

questions.question: How should the PN send a urine specimen to the laboratory?
options: In a labeled, sealed container inside a biohazard bag
In the client's water pitcher with a lid
In an open cup carried by hand to the lab
Unlabeled, with the label added later
questions.explanation: Specimens are labeled at the bedside in front of the client and transported in a sealed biohazard bag to protect staff and ensure accuracy.

questions.question: A client has a red allergy wristband. What does the PN confirm before giving any medication?
options: The client's insurance plan and payment status
The client's room number and the physician's name
The client's allergies and the reactions listed in the record
The client's favorite foods and the visiting hours
questions.explanation: Checking allergies against each medication before giving it prevents allergic reactions, which can be life-threatening.

questions.question: The PN finds a client on the floor beside the bed. What should the PN do first?
options: Call the family to tell them about the fall before you assess the client
Check the client for injury and call for help before moving them
Help the client back to bed right away before anyone else sees what happened
Complete an incident report before examining the client or calling for any help
questions.explanation: The client is checked for injuries such as head trauma or fractures before being moved. The RN and provider are notified, and the fall is documented.

questions.question: A client receiving oxygen by nasal cannula wants to use an electric razor. What should the PN do?
options: Suggest a safety razor or check facility policy on electrical devices
Allow it and turn the oxygen up to compensate for the electrical device in the room
Allow it while the client smokes near the oxygen because the razor is quiet
Remove the oxygen permanently for the shave
questions.explanation: Sparks from electrical devices near oxygen are a fire risk. Many facilities restrict electric razors for clients using oxygen.

questions.question: A client is admitted with suspected pertussis. Which PPE should the PN put on before entering the room?
options: A sterile gown
No PPE beyond hand hygiene
An N95 respirator only
A surgical mask
questions.explanation: Pertussis spreads by droplets, so a surgical mask is worn in addition to standard precautions.

questions.question: Which statement by an assistive personnel about using a mechanical lift shows the need for more teaching?
options: "I'll lock the wheels of the bed."
"I'll do this lift alone to save time."
"I'll explain each step to the client."
"I'll check the sling for tears before using it."
questions.explanation: Most mechanical lifts require two staff members for safety. Working alone increases the risk of falls and injuries.

questions.question: A child accidentally swallows a parent's pills. What should the parent do first?
options: Give the child milk and wait to see what happens
Make the child vomit right away at home
Wait to see if symptoms develop before calling anyone, since many pills are harmless
Call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) or 911 if the child is unresponsive
questions.explanation: Poison Control gives specific advice. Inducing vomiting is no longer recommended at home because it can cause harm.

questions.question: The PN is reinforcing hand hygiene teaching with a client's family. Which statement shows understanding?
options: "I'll rub the alcohol gel over all my hand surfaces until dry."
"A quick rinse with water is enough."
"Gloves mean I never need to clean my hands."
"I'll wipe my hands on my pants after using gel so they dry faster."
questions.explanation: Alcohol rub must cover all hand surfaces and be rubbed until dry to be effective.

questions.question: Which client is at the highest risk for falls?
options: An alert teenager with a cold, a runny nose, and a sore throat who is walking
A young adult walking steadily after a dental procedure under local anesthesia
An older adult who takes a diuretic and a sleeping pill and gets up at night to void
A middle-aged adult with a sprained wrist who uses a cane
questions.explanation: Advanced age, nighttime urgency, and sedating medications combine to greatly increase fall risk.

questions.question: A client's IV site is red and warm, and the client has a fever. Which action should the PN take?
options: Flush the catheter harder to clear the redness and push out the infection
Ignore it since fever is common after surgery and usually goes away on its own
Report the findings to the RN, who will plan to remove the catheter
Apply a new dressing over the old one and check the site again in the morning
questions.explanation: Redness, warmth, and fever suggest a catheter-related infection. The PN reports promptly so the device can be removed and the client evaluated.

questions.question: A resident has a fever and diarrhea, and two other residents on the same hall have similar symptoms. What should the PN do?
options: Give antidiarrheal medicine to all residents on the hall
Report it to the RN and infection prevention promptly; use contact precautions
Wait until more residents become sick before reporting it to anyone on the team
Move the sick residents into one room together without waiting for any orders from the RN
questions.explanation: A cluster of similar symptoms may be an outbreak. Prompt reporting and contact precautions help limit the spread.

questions.question: During a fire on the unit, clients have been rescued and the alarm has been activated. Which action is part of the 'Contain' step of RACE?
options: Turning off clients' oxygen without checking them
Taking the elevator to the ground floor
Opening windows to let out smoke
Closing doors and windows to the area
questions.explanation: Containing the fire means closing doors and windows to limit the spread of smoke and flames. Elevators are not used during a fire.

questions.question: The PN is caring for a client on airborne precautions. Which action requires the PN to intervene?
options: An assistive personnel enters wearing a surgical mask
The client wears a surgical mask while being transported
The door to the room is kept closed
Staff put on fit-tested N95 respirators before entering
questions.explanation: Airborne precautions require a fit-tested N95 respirator or higher. A surgical mask does not protect staff from airborne particles.

questions.question: A provider writes an order for wrist restraints 'as needed' (PRN) for a confused client. What should the PN do?
options: Apply the restraints at night only when staff is short
Apply the restraints whenever the client seems restless
Ask the RN to clarify the order, since restraint orders cannot be PRN
Ask the family whether to use the restraints or not
questions.explanation: Restraint orders must be time-limited and specific, and PRN orders are not permitted. Restraints are a last resort after less restrictive measures.

questions.question: Which action by the PN is most important to prevent an infection in a client with an indwelling urinary catheter?
options: Letting the bag drag on the floor while walking
Keeping the drainage bag below the bladder and the system closed
Raising the bag onto the bed during transfers
Opening the system to take samples at the bedside whenever the provider asks
questions.explanation: A closed system and gravity drainage keep urine from flowing back into the bladder and reduce infection risk.

questions.question: A client returns from a procedure and needs to be moved from a stretcher to the bed. Which action shows safe practice?
options: Using a slide board or friction-reducing device with enough staff
Asking the client to jump onto the bed without any help
Pulling the client by the arms to slide over the sheet
Lifting the client alone to save time and staff effort
questions.explanation: Assistive devices and adequate staff reduce injuries to both the client and the nursing staff.

questions.question: During a disaster drill, an assistive personnel asks why staff practice evacuation routes. Which response by the PN is best?
options: "It is just a requirement with no real purpose and is only for the inspectors."
"Only managers and supervisors need to know the evacuation routes in this building."
"We will use the elevators during a real fire because they are the fastest way out."
"Practice helps everyone respond quickly and safely in a real emergency."
questions.explanation: Drills prepare staff to act quickly during real emergencies. Elevators should not be used during a fire.

questions.question: A client receiving a continuous tube feeding suddenly starts coughing and has trouble breathing. What should the PN do first?
options: Increase the feeding rate to finish the feeding sooner and clear the airway
Stop the feeding, keep the head of the bed up, and report to the RN
Flush the tube with 60 mL of water and restart the feeding right away
Lower the head of the bed flat to ease coughing
questions.explanation: Coughing and dyspnea during a feeding suggest aspiration. Stopping the feeding prevents more formula from entering the airway, and the RN must assess the client right away.
